output.brief: The rise in falls at the two homes can't yet be pinned on the night rota. Three things changed at the same time: the rota (June), the incident app (July) and the GP practice and admission mix (May to summer). The app go-live matters most. Before July, falls came from paper forms. A check of Q2 handover notes found at least three unreported falls in just 6 of 13 weeks, and three more that might be falls. Unwitnessed "found on floor" falls rose from 5 to 14, mostly with no harm, which fits better recording. On the rate chart, both homes' Q3 rates are within their long-run ranges. Five other single-home rises of 70% or more in the group fell back without any action. That doesn't rule out a real rise, because the chart is slow to detect one. There are no call-bell times from before June, so slower answering can't be shown. My advice: keep the pilot under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates and mark the change in reporting method. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times now. Review in late January with Q4 data. Don't issue capability warnings, and don't go back to paper. My confidence is moderate.
